name: Blastocystis spp.

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Common vacuolar forms are approximately 5–30 µm, with a large central body and a thin cytoplasmic rim containing nuclei.
Granular and other forms occur; preservation can substantially alter appearance.

transmission.detail: Fecal-oral transmission is implicated; intestinal stages are shed, with cyst forms contributing to transmission.

life_cycle.detail: Fecal-oral transmission is implicated; intestinal stages are shed, with cyst forms contributing to transmission.
Vacuolar and other forms in stool; use stage-qualified labels.

hosts: Humans and many animals; host association varies by subtype. No established intermediate host.
distribution: Worldwide and frequently detected in Southeast Asian surveys.
clinical_significance: Often asymptomatic; clinical significance is variable and debated. Detection alone does not establish the cause of gastrointestinal symptoms.
specimen: Vacuolar and other forms in stool; use stage-qualified labels.
diagnostics: Wet mounts and permanent stained smears at 400–1000×; molecular analysis identifies subtypes.
differential_diagnosis: Fat droplets, yeast and degenerating cells can mimic vacuolar forms; subtypes cannot be assigned by routine morphology.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated
description: Blastocystis spp. — Blastocystis intestinal protist. Often asymptomatic; clinical significance is variable and debated. Detection alone does not establish the cause of gastrointestinal symptoms.

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
